title: ELIZA—A Computer Program for the Study of Natural Language Communication Between Man and Machine
summary: Joseph Weizenbaum published ELIZA—A Computer Program for the Study of Natural Language Communication Between Man and Machine in Communications of the ACM in January 1966, documenting ELIZA operating within MIT's MAC time-sharing system and conducting natural-language dialogue through keyword-triggered decomposition rules.
significance: A documented early conversational-computing and natural-language-processing system in the history of human-computer dialogue.

verification.note: The ACM Digital Library publisher record directly supports the title, Joseph Weizenbaum as author, his Massachusetts Institute of Technology affiliation, Communications of the ACM volume 9 issue 1, pages 36-45, DOI 10.1145/365153.365168, and January 1966 publication. The ACM article description states that ELIZA operated within MIT's MAC time-sharing system and analyzed input using decomposition rules triggered by keywords. Month precision is retained even though ACM's publication-history interface displays 1 January 1966, so LINEAiGE does not turn a publisher-interface day into a separate claim about the program's invention or release date. MIT is recorded as publisher-supported author affiliation/context, not inferred development geography. ACM is retained as publisher provenance rather than represented as a participating organization. No ancestry, influence, causality, or relationship edges are inferred.
